items.title: Extensions of modules over the base glue from I-power torsion extensions after a flat covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat ring map R -> S and a finitely generated ideal I with R/I -> S/IS an isomorphism, and says that for R-modules M and N with M being I-power torsion, every short exact sequence 0 -> N tensor_R S -> E-tilde -> M tensor_R S -> 0 descends to a commutative diagram of short exact sequences over R (source lines 24476-24501). The proof reformulates the statement as the assertion that the base-change map Ext_R(M, N) -> Ext_S(M tensor_R S, N tensor_R S) is an isomorphism, and it proves the stronger isomorphism statement. The reduction is a genuine chain: since M is I-power torsion one has M tensor_R S = M; the base-change map on Ext is functorial because R -> S is flat (proof lines 24504-24515). Choosing by the presentation lemma a surjection M' -> M with M' a direct sum of modules R/I^n, the six-term exact sequence together with the neighbourhood equivalence reduces the claim to M' and then, using compatibility of Ext with direct sums in a step the author states is omitted, to the single case M = R/I^n (proof lines 24518-24526). The case M = R/I^n is done by writing f_1, ..., f_t for generators of I^n and using the explicit description of Ext in terms of Koszul homology: the proof displays a commutative diagram with exact rows relating Ext_R(R/I^n, N) to H_1(N, f_bullet) and Hom_R(K, N), where K is the module of the naive Koszul complex, and reduces to showing the two right-hand vertical arrows are isomorphisms (proof lines 24529-24546). That is then verified directly: Hom_R(K, N) = Hom_S(K tensor_R S, N tensor_R S) because K is annihilated by I^n, and H_1(N, f_bullet) tensor_R S = H_1(N tensor_R S, f_bullet) = H_1(N, f_bullet) because R -> S is flat and H_1(N, f_bullet) is annihilated by I^n (proof lines 24547-24555). The non-routine content is the reduction to M = R/I^n and the Koszul-homology comparison that finishes it.
